index_description_first_line: Want to send something private? A password, love-note or something else, no-one else than the recipient should see?
index_description_bullet_point_1: Encrypt your message in your browser with a randomly generated password.
index_description_bullet_point_2: Upload the encrypted message to the server (while not sharing the password with the server)
index_description_bullet_point_3: Display the password as well as a link to get the message back, which you can then share with your recipient.
index_error_creating_drop: There was an error creating your drop. Please try again.
index_drop_made_description: Your recipient needs the link as well as the password to get the drop. It might be best to just fully copy the message below to your recipient.
drop_message_2_kicker: I'm sending you some secure data that you can fetch here:
drop_message_6_description_1: This link will only work once, so be careful with the password, and make sure to copy the data immediately.
drop_message_7_description_2: After you pick it up (either successfully or with e.g. a wrong password), the data will self-destruct and won't be available anymore.
drop_message_8_description_3_time: This link will only work for %1$d hours, after that, the data will self-destruct as well.
info_kicker: Here are the steps this platform does with your message:
info_bullet_point_1_after_link: , the message is encrypted in your browser with a password generated in your browser.
info_bullet_point_2: This means, that the data does not leave your browser unencrypted, as well as your password.
info_bullet_point_3: The encrypted data is then sent to the backend, where it is stored for a maximum of %1$d hours (or when the drop is fetched, whichever is earlier).
info_bullet_point_4: When getting the drop, the encrypted data is fetched from the server (and instantly deleted when doing so), and is only encrypted in the browser. So, also here, the inserted password never leaves the browser.
info_bullet_point_5: So the server (we) cannot see your message, as we never get the password for it.
info_encryption_after_link: , which is a JavaScript crypto library developed at Stanford.
info_open_source_after_link: , and you can easily inspect what is going on on this website with your developer tools.
info_self_host_before_link: Furthermore, feel free to host your
info_self_host_after_link: , so that we do not even get to see your encrypted data at any time, so that you do not have to rely on us not trying to decrypt your data.
pickup_kicker: Enter the password you got provided with this link.
pickup_description_before_button_text: This will only work once! Clicking
pickup_description_after_button_text: will delete the message permanently, regardless of whether the password was correct or not.
pickup_error_description_kicker: There was an error getting your drop. This can either be:
pickup_error_description_bullet_point_1: The drop has already been fetched. You can only open / get a drop once. If you didn't get the drop yet, it might be that someone else tried (and if they got the password, may have succeeded) to get your drop. If you are unsure, you should consider that the dropped content is no longer safe in this scenario.
pickup_error_description_bullet_point_2: The entered password was wrong. You can only open / get a drop once, and if you enter the wrong password, the drop is gone forever. If you didn't get the drop yet, it might be that someone else tried (and if they got the password, may have succeeded) to get your drop. If you are unsure, you should consider that the dropped content is no longer safe in this scenario.
pickup_error_description_bottom_line: In each case, if neither you nor the creator of the drop took actions that could lead to this scenario, please consider that the content of your drop may be in malicious hands as of now.
html_meta_description: Create one-time links for securely sending data
